about: The corpus of the guard hook (T133). Bash commands of a bridge session: 'refuse' (not on the allow-list), 'broker' (GitHub: refused with the hint to the sage-bot broker tools of the session), 'state' (the sage state tool in any form: refused with the stop ending), 'wildcard' (a wildcard in a pipeline that runs or writes that may match the state tool, or any [ there, and in an operand that git or node --test expands as a pattern, a quoted one too: refused with the hint to name the files), 'pattern' (any other character than letters, digits, a space and _ - . / , : = % ~ ^ * ? in such an operand, such as @, +, (, { or \: refused with the stop ending, F-T133-51), 'allow' (normal developer commands), 'sandbox' (allowed by the hook; the Claude Code sandbox and the permission rules of step 6 hold their files and hosts). 'tools' are calls of the other tools as [tool, input]. 'slow' (F-T133-62) are forms of a wildcard word that a backtracking match took minutes to decide: the test fills {STARS} with 48 stars and with 64 KB of wildcard shapes, and each must decide in under 1 s. 'session' is a realistic sage session in order: every call must be allowed.
refuse: gh pr merge 12 # just a view
git push origin feature；gh pr merge 12
osascript -e 'tell app "Terminal" to do script "gh pr merge 12"'
broker: gh pr create --title 'T133: guard' --body 'The guard hook.'
allow: git add README.md && git commit -m x
git commit -m "T133 R493: class rules for quoted patterns, pipelines and /dev/"

worktree.about: Bash commands in a worktree under .claude/worktrees/<name> (EnterWorktree makes them), the cwd below. 'refuse': a write that lands in a settings folder from there, by .., an = in a folder name, ~+ or a quoted ~ (F-T137-L1, F-T137-9), also with a quoted variable in front (T200), a message option before it (T202), a -C folder that starts with --message= (F-T199-3) or after --amend (T203); 'hint': [command, the hint, a form that the hint leads to]: the command is refused with the hint, and the form is allowed from the same cwd (F-T137-8, F-T137-12, F-T137-14, F-T137-15; T199: a cd up into .claude; T200: a quoted variable gets the hint of the form with no quotes); 'allow': normal work there, also a message that starts with ~ or names .claude (T202; also --message <text>, F-T199-4) and git commit --amend and --no-edit (T203). 'parent' holds the same for a shell in .claude/worktrees itself, after an allowed cd .. && ls (F-T137-13).
